editorial:
Imagine three groups of crooks living on the exact same Brooklyn street, but each group thinks they are starring in a completely different kind of movie. That is the wild setup here, and it is a blast from the very first scene. The Amateurs act like they stepped out of a gritty 1970s crime flick, the Sputniks move through their world in black and white, and the Moolies are stuck living like they are in a flashy rap video. You watch these three styles crash into each other, and the result is funny, strange, and surprisingly charming. The movie never takes itself too seriously, which makes it easy to sit back and enjoy the ride.

The acting is energetic across the board, and the action scenes are staged with a playful wink rather than heavy seriousness. Pacing stays quick, though a few jokes land harder than others, and the genre mashup can feel a little chaotic at times. Still, if you enjoy crime comedies with a clever twist, this one delivers. Stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for your collection. It is a fun pick for a relaxed movie night with friends.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, the three criminal teams finally collide during one big heist on the shared block. Their separate movie worlds blend together, and the walls between the 1970s crime drama, black and white noir, and rap video styles break down completely. The twist reveals that all three groups were part of the same larger plan all along, and the heist succeeds in a messy but satisfying way. Everyone walks away with their share, and the movie ends on a playful note that ties the genres together.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves crime comedies and clever genre mashups.
